clue.text: Idiot losing head gets one in the eye

indicators.note: losing its head means the idiot word drops its first letter

parts.note: a cretin is an idiot
a means one

explanation.surface: A fool who has been decapitated gets one in the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a part found in the eye, not a synonym of 'in the eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive membrane at the back of the eyeball is found in the eye.

clue.text: With lots of pebbles around, striking in a loud aggressive way

indicators.note: the pebbly word sits around the striking word

parts.note: shingly describes a beach covered with lots of pebbles
workers who are striking are out

explanation.surface: Someone surrounded by pebbles hits out in a loud and aggressive manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like hitting but means on strike, i.e. OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something while shouting is doing it loudly and aggressively.

clue.text: Flutter I make with a bit of a blackberry, say

definitions.text: a bit of a blackberry, say

indicators.note: make signals that the letters of Flutter and I are made into something new

explanation.surface: A person nervously makes something from a fragment of blackberry.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackberry is a cluster of tiny fruits, each one a drupelet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruitlet is one small fruit within a compound fruit, like each little bead of a blackberry.

clue.text: See 25
Candidates for ASBO by and by?

definitions.text: Candidates for ASBO by and by?

indicators.note: candidates for are things that could become something, so the letters may be rearranged into it

explanation.surface: Asks whether certain people will eventually qualify for an antisocial behaviour order.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO is a British antisocial behaviour order. Rearranging ASBO, BY and BY gives the answer; the whole clue jokes that infant boys will grow up into yobs deserving one.
explanation.definitionFit: Infant boys might in time grow into troublemakers eligible for an antisocial behaviour order.

clue.text: Standard round of journeys around French capital Henry VI didn't reach

parts.note: par is a standard or norm

indicators.note: the journey word goes around the French initial

parts.note: a tour is a round of journeys

indicators.note: the capital, or initial letter, of French

explanation.surface: Instructions about a standard trip around France's capital, mixed with a remark about a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Henry VI has three parts, so a fourth was never written.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote Henry VI in three parts, so its fourth section is what the play never reached.

clue.text: Number making saint's detailed numbers include practical method for transport round curves …

indicators.note: de-tailed: the saint's name loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: St Theresa (of Avila or Lisieux) is the saint

indicators.note: the numbers word holds the practical word within it

parts.note: businesslike means practical and efficient
how a thing is done is its method

indicators.note: the vehicle word goes round the curves word

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport
sines are the curves of trigonometry

explanation.surface: A rambling instruction about a saint's figures and a way of getting a vehicle round bends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a song: Irving Berlin's showbiz anthem, hinted at by the clue running on into 9-across. The saint's name loses its A to give the contracted opening word with its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song in a show, and this is Irving Berlin's famous showbiz anthem from Annie Get Your Gun.

clue.text: Look to do what a cat may?

definitions.text: Look to do what a cat may?

parts.words: Look to do what a cat may?
parts.note: a cat may look at a king, so to look at K is the cat's privilege; and to look for something is to try for it

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a cat may look at a king' is the key: SEE + K (king).
explanation.definitionFit: To look for or try to find something is a plain synonym, and the cat sees a king.

clue.text: Fall into this and you'll be t___

definitions.text: Fall into this and you'll be t___

parts.words: Fall into this and you'll be t___
parts.note: the gap after t needs a word that completes something you'd be after a fall into a kiln for drying hops

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank with the answer and t___ becomes TOAST: you would be, if you fell into a hop kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, hot enough that a fall into one would roast you.

clue.text: … with capital responsible for it

explanation.surface: The run-on from the previous clue names a capital city as the author of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 6-across: the capital of Germany shares its name with Irving Berlin, who wrote that song.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany's capital city; also the surname of songwriter Irving Berlin, who composed the song in 6-across.

clue.text: See 6
Polish ring round 'ead and beak to be a showman

parts.note: to buff is to polish
a ring round the head is a halo; the dropped H of 'ead asks for it said the Cockney way, without its H
a bird's beak is its bill

explanation.surface: Someone polishes a ring around a head and a beak to become an entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ead is the signal: a halo, said by someone who drops their aitches, loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cody, known as Buffalo Bill, ran the famous Wild West touring show, making him a showman.

clue.text: Blurred Oxford gent has nothing on coppers

parts.note: OU is Oxford University
a toff is a posh gent
O is zero, nothing
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, made plural

explanation.surface: An Oxford gentleman is wearing nothing but a few policemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police but is the chemical element, its symbol Cu pluralised.
explanation.definitionFit: An image that is out of focus is blurred, lacking sharpness.

clue.text: Single member allowed? It doesn't say

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single
an MP is a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: Is one MP permitted? The rules are silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied rather than stated outright, so it doesn't say.

clue.text: Drink for girl 24 and group, say

indicators.note: say signals the words spoken out loud

parts.note: the girl with a gun is Annie, of Annie Get Your Gun; a group is a set

explanation.surface: Ordering a drink for a young woman and her gang.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' refers to the light WITH A GUN: Irving Berlin's Annie Get Your Gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, a kind of drink.

clue.text: Ingenuity missing in Guantanamo: watch out! Shooting doesn't work

indicators.note: out signals the letters breaking loose from their order
missing tells us the little word in is taken away from Ingenuity

parts.note: the word in, as written

explanation.surface: A warning that cleverness is absent at a notorious prison camp, where gunfire achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IN from INGENUITY to leave GENUITY; with GUANTANAMO and WATCH that makes 22 letters to rearrange, as 'out' instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irving Berlin song title from Annie Get Your Gun says that firearms are no way to win a husband, so shooting fails.

clue.text: Topless sort of philosophy? Well!

indicators.note: topless means the philosophy word loses its first letter

parts.note: Cartesian philosophy is that of Descartes

explanation.surface: A remark about stripped-off philosophy, followed by an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well!' looks like an exclamation but means a kind of water source; the answer is the adjective for that kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well is one where water rises under its own pressure, so the word names a type of well.

clue.text: See 15
Stick with these gentleman-like pupils

parts.note: toffy, a variant spelling, means like a toff, a posh gentleman
the pupil of the eye is called its apple

explanation.surface: Advice to stay loyal to a group of refined schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupils' look like schoolchildren but are the apples of the eye. TOFFY is an accepted variant spelling of the confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee-coated apples are sold on sticks, so a stick is what goes with them.

clue.text: Leave car at home with cake

parts.note: to park is to leave a car
in means at home

explanation.surface: Advice to leave the car outside and stay home with cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Parkin is a ginger cake made with oatmeal and treacle, from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a kind of sticky oatmeal gingerbread, a traditional northern English cake.

clue.text: Disappointment? Puff needed

explanation.surface: Something disappointing needs a puff of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a blow; to puff out air is to blow.

clue.text: Satirical presentation of St Christopher

parts.note: S is short for saint
Kit is a pet form of the name Christopher

explanation.surface: A comic sketch about the patron saint of travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic or satirical sketch or performance.

clue.text: See 6
Playwright has gap without a model

indicators.note: without means the gap word goes on minus the letter a

parts.note: a breach is a gap, as in a wall
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A dramatist has a gap in his life because he lacks a model.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertolt Brecht was the German dramatist who wrote Mother Courage and The Threepenny Opera.

clue.text: See 15
Shepherdess getting letters to be involved with Pole — and letter

parts.note: Litt. is the abbreviation for letters (Litterarum), as in the degree D.Litt.

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of be and Pole are jumbled together

parts.note: Ep. is the abbreviation for epistle, a letter

explanation.surface: A shepherdess acquires academic qualifications so she can be linked with a Pole, plus a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' scrambles BE and POLE into LEBOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme shepherdess who has lost her sheep and doesn't know where to find them.
